title: Shriner tour prank with Beiersdorffer's band
summary: A Shriners tour with Johnny Bayersdorffer's band in which pranksters stuffed his tuba with towels and cheese.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: I was waking with Johnny Byerstoff at the Tokyo Garden. And he, you see, his father used to be a swine in the Sharmogrot. The Sharmogrot of the Sharmogrot. Well, he was one himself. Byerstoffer. Yeah, Byerstoffer, the trumpet player. That was before he went off and he left the city, see. So, naturally his dad had got our band to go and travel all around the country with the Shriners. They had made a tour all around the country with the Shriners, see. So, every time that we would go in a different city, we'd have to get off the train and the band and pray to get the Shriners together, see. To receive the new delegates that was coming on, see. So, I don't forget what city it was. We stopped there and we got off. And I had that great big tour that I used to have, you know. That's Harry BJ. That bell was that big one. I had it especially made. The tour was a Suzaphone. Suzaphone.
It was a Suzaphone, see. Is that a double B-flat?

No, E-flat. But it was a double E. It was a double E, see. Big one. Yeah. So, we got off in this special city. I don't remember where it was. And like I said, we got the plan to get the new delegates in there, you know. So, the band is playing. And I see old man Biles Stoffer. He's looking at me like that, you know. He's doing this, you see. He don't say nothing, you see. Got through playing. He said, Jim, do you feelin' alright? I said, yeah, why? He says, I don't know. He says, but I don't hear that tuba. And boy, if I do say that I was young, at that time I had win. Yeah. Because I played it with, what, 16, 20 men. You could hear that tuba above the band. Anybody can tell you that. Because I used to have a wonderful pair of lungs if I did say it myself. And he says, I don't hear the tuba, Chink. I look at him, I says, are you kidding, Mr. Biles Stoffer? He says, no, Chink. He says, no, Chink. He says, there's nothing comin' out of it. Man, I start to get worried. I look at him like that. Took the mouthpiece off. I had to get laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid laid I look at him and I say, are you kidding Mr. Beistoffer? He says, no, Chank. He says, there's nothing coming out of it. Man, I start to get worried. I start rubbing my lip like that. I look in the mouthpiece like that. I took the mouthpiece off. I took the slightest. Good grief. I said, don't tell me I'm breaking down. You see? Because I could see he was serious about it, you know? So I took the God-doin' thing off my neck and I put it down. See? Like that. And then I don't know what's making it. And I look down at the two of them. There's a big four of them. Two of them! Come on! Oh! Oh! Oh! Oh, man, Beist. I can't stand this no more. He says, that's no way to treat this man. This man, this man is blowing his lungs out there. Nothing coming out. Look at what. Who done this? He tried to fly. You could never fly. I don't die. Because I had it on the corner of the coach, you know? With the belt. You know, that corner right there. You know what he'd done? He just had to throw towels in there and shove them in with the head, you know? And I was blowing like that. Because to tell you the truth, I couldn't hear it myself. But I figured maybe it was my ears or something. The towels! And no wonder he couldn't hear it. And then, the entire time, the leg caught me. And I leave something that I never do. I leave the mouthpiece on the horn. And he takes a limb-boigert cheese and fills the mouthpiece with limb-boigert cheese. And naturally, sometimes, you know how we are in a hurry. All right, let's go. Grab that and I'll grab that and put it to my-
No, boy! No, no, no, no. You know, man, I'm telling you, them fellas used to play rough. Yeah.
